analyst.summary: ABB India's order book has re-accelerated sharply for three straight quarters (Q4 CY2025 +52%, Q1 CY2026 +25%, and a parent-disclosed Q2 CY2026 India read-through of +81% that sent the stock to a fresh record high on 16 July 2026), but delivered revenue growth has stayed stuck at 6-8% for over a year and PBT margin has compressed from 21% to 16.2-16.9% on cost and competitive pressures -- a genuine, multi-quarter deceleration that is part base-effect (an unsustainable 2022-2024 supercycle), part real margin/cost cycle, and part order-to-revenue conversion lag, rather than a single cause. Earnings quality needs care: Q1 CY2026's headline profit jump was almost entirely a Rs 1,658 crore one-off gain on the since-completed Robotics divestment, masking a roughly 25% YoY decline in core operating profit and artificially depressing the naive trailing P/E. At a core/recurring multiple of roughly 86-99x trailing (76-88x forward CY27E) against a 75%-promoter-held, 25%-free-float register, the stock is priced for growth and margin recovery that the 31 July 2026 results (a live, ~13-day event window) have not yet confirmed -- sell-side already delivered one real re-rating scare in May 2026 (a 10% single-day drop, multiple Sell ratings). No balance-sheet or governance flags, and order momentum argues against selling strength, but valuation offers no margin of safety if the upcoming print disappoints on margins even as orders beat.
